picks.style: sanskrit philosophical recitation, tanpura drone, hand cymbals, deep male voice, slow, austere, cutting
picks.why: The one flash of scorn in the whole treatise: a man who cannot hold a hair's tip in his belly says all this was done by me — and who is more deluded than one who fancies himself learned?

picks.style: vedic-style chant, drone, low male voices in unison, no percussion, very slow, expansive
picks.why: The śruti passage carried inside it — that alone is fire, that the sun, that the wind, that the moon — pure anaphora, built for chanting.

picks.style: gita recitation setting, tanpura and bansuri, warm male voice, measured, contemplative
picks.why: Three Gītā verses in a row on the constituents doing the acting while the deluded self says I am the agent — the most quotable material present.

picks.style: urdu ghazal, harmonium, tabla, sitar, expressive male vocal, rubato, yearning, intimate
picks.why: Lightning, moon, ocean, shore — then the turn: I am the merchant who has found his profit in despair. Every couplet stands alone.

picks.style: urdu nazm, bansuri and sitar, soft tanpura, hushed male voice, very slow, nocturnal
picks.why: Iqbal's evening poem entire: the stream stilled, the bell-less caravan of stars, and the last line telling the heart to take its sorrow into sleep.

picks.style: urdu song for young voices, light harmonium and dholak, bright unison chorus, lilting, walking pace
picks.why: The stars complaining to the moon, with a built-in refrain — to journey, journey, ever on.

picks.style: scottish pastoral ballad, harp and fiddle, tenor voice, slow, nocturnal, elegiac
picks.why: The Hermit's opening — hamlet still, torrent on the hill, nightingale in the grove — a poem already famous as a song in its own century.

picks.style: scottish air, clarsach, low strings, tenor, unhurried, mournful, spacious
picks.why: The moon rolls on and returns to splendour; man's faded glory does not. Ends on the mouldering urn and the gloom of the grave.

picks.style: georgian ode, chamber strings, chamber organ, clear tenor, gentle, twilight, flowing
picks.why: Shook from the purple wings of Even — short alternating lines, a star of love, a plaintive stream. Perfect ballad-metre singing shape.

picks.style: 18th-century catch, harpsichord and cello, jaunty male trio, quick, playful, tavern
picks.why: Little tube of mighty pow'r, lip of wax and eye of fire — the most quoted lines Browne wrote, in tight singable tetrameter.

picks.style: georgian glee, harpsichord, viols, warm baritone, mid-tempo, wry, convivial
picks.why: The mock-Pope panegyric to tobacco, ending on the famous line about tasting it unexcis'd by kings.

picks.style: english baroque ode, flute and harpsichord, light soprano, graceful, moderate, bright
picks.why: Come, rosy Health, celestial maid — a clean invocation with a rolling catalogue of rural attendants.

picks.style: vedic hymn, tanpura drone, deep male chant, sparse frame drum, very slow, reverent
picks.why: The Hiraṇyagarbha hymn with its returning question — what god shall we adore with our oblations? — five times over. A refrain already built in.

picks.style: cosmic invocation, low drone, layered male voices, no percussion, hushed, vast, weightless
picks.why: The creation hymn: neither being nor not-being, darkness hidden in darkness, and desire as the first germ of mind.

picks.style: upanishadic chant, tanpura, soft bell, single voice with distant echo, slow, luminous
picks.why: The two birds on one tree — one eating the sweet berries, the other only gazing — the single most memorable image in the Upanishads.

picks.style: late-romantic art song, solo piano, dramatic baritone, rubato, by turns mocking and tender
picks.why: Gazing into Life's eye and sinking; she pulls him out with a golden angle and laughs. A complete dramatic scene between two figures.

picks.style: chamber lied, piano and low strings, weary baritone, slow, dusk-lit, questioning
picks.why: Ends on the evening's interrogation — why, wherefore, whither, how — and the sun long set over a damp meadow.

picks.style: medieval latin chant, male schola, bare drone, no percussion, solemn, slow
picks.why: The only verse in the passage — the fruitful land bringing forth Alban, and the snake of envy reared against Augustine.

picks.style: greek tragic chorus, lyre, aulos, layered male voices, solemn, questioning, building
picks.why: A whole self-contained Euripidean stanza on mortals understanding nothing and depending wholly on Zeus.
